facts.fact: Adwave's article states that by 2026 global ad spending is predicted to cross the $1 trillion mark for the first time.
facts.quote: By **2026**, it's predicted that global ad spending will cross the **$1 trillion** mark for the very first time.

facts.fact: Adwave's article says the first three seconds of an ad determine whether viewers keep watching.
facts.quote: The priority is won or lost in the first three seconds. If you can't give someone a compelling reason to keep watching right away

facts.fact: Adwave's article says the hook section of a 30-second spot gets about five seconds.
facts.quote: You’ve got a scant five seconds to grab someone.

facts.fact: Adwave's article says the problem-and-solution section of a 30-second spot gets about 20 seconds, spanning seconds 6-25.
facts.quote: Now you have about **20 seconds** to build on it.

facts.fact: Adwave's article says the call-to-action section of a 30-second spot gets the last five seconds.
facts.quote: These last five seconds might be the most important.

facts.fact: Adwave's article describes the 30-second spot as the heavyweight of broadcast advertising, without giving a market-share figure.
facts.quote: The **30-second** spot is the undisputed heavyweight of broadcast advertising.

facts.fact: Adwave's article describes a 6-second bumper ad as a format whose primary goal is instant brand recall rather than storytelling.
facts.quote: The 6-second "bumper" ad is even more of a creative challenge. It’s all about rapid-fire impact.

facts.fact: The global advertising market is projected to reach $1.14 trillion in 2025, according to the page (no source is named).
facts.quote: The global advertising market is projected to hit a staggering **$1.14 trillion** in 2025

facts.fact: For a standard 30-second spot, the page recommends a script between 65 and 75 words.
facts.quote: For a standard **30-second** spot, you'll want to aim for a script that's between **65 and 75 words**.

facts.fact: The page says a 65-75 word script for a 30-second spot creates a pace of about 2.5 words per second.
facts.quote: creates a comfortable, natural pace (about 2.5 words per second)

facts.fact: The page describes the two-column script, also called an Audio/Video (AV) script, as the go-to format in the industry, with video on the left and audio on the right.
facts.quote: The go-to format in the industry is the **two-column script**, sometimes called an Audio/Video (AV) script.
